title: Regional circuit-breaker & canary traffic-shift playbook (draft)
content:
TL;DR:
This is a working draft runbook for handling region-level degradations where we use an automated circuit-breaker policy at the edge plus a staged canary traffic shift (DNS weight + routing controls) to warm-standby regions. Goal: keep customer-facing latency and error-rate SLOs within acceptable bounds while minimizing blast radius and avoiding cache/traffic storms.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies when a single cloud region (or equivalent AZ-cluster group) becomes degraded (network blackhole, region-level API failures, or severe backend error spike).
- We assume warm-standby regions are up-to-date with model weights and KV caches warm enough for baseline throughput.
- This runbook focuses on multi-region traffic steering, DNS weight changes, BGP/community hints, and service-level circuit-breaker adjustments (Envoy/ingress level).
- Not a replacement for postmortems; use with incident commander (IC) and SRE lead.

Metrics to watch (dashboard names):
- frontend/errors/5xx-rate (p95 over 1m, 5m)
- frontend/latency/p95 (global and per-region)
- edge/active-conns and edge/request-rate per region
- model-serving/kv-hit-rate and model-serving/latency p95
- route53/weight-failover events (audit logs)

Pre-incident checklist (prep, do this weekly):
- Validate Route53 health checks for primary and warm-standby (expected status = success)
- Verify DNS TTLs for region A records are <= 60s for critical hostnames used in failover
- Confirm BGP announcements automation (if using direct-provisioned network) is tested in staging
- Run a dry-run canary: 1% weight shift to standby region during low traffic window; check latency and cache-miss amplification
- Ensure infractl credentials are accessible to on-call (k/v store path: /secrets/ops/infractl)

Quick glossary:
- Canary shift: staged change of traffic weight to standby (Route53 weighted records + proxy routing rules).
- Circuit-breaker: service-level policy to isolate/stop forwarding requests to unhealthy backends (timeouts, max connections, consecutive 5xx triggers).
- Warm-standby: region kept warm with minimum replicas, periodic cache warming jobs, and model parity.

Detection & triage (first 10 minutes):
1) IC confirms region health degradation: cross-check region metrics + external monitoring (Datadog synthetic checks).
2) Determine if degradation is network-only or service-level: run traceroutes and curl health endpoints from multiple regions: 
   - curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api-us-east.redwood.ai/health || echo "network failure"
3) If region returns >5% 5xx or p95 latency > SLO for 5m, escalate to SRE on-call and runbook owner.

Decision matrix (fast):
- If metric breach < 5 minutes and no confirmed control-plane issue: set circuit-breaker to conservative (reduce concurrency, increase timeout), monitor 5m.
- If sustained >10 minutes or partial traffic blackholes observed: start canary shift (1->5->25->100% weights) with 5-10 minute observation windows.
- If BGP or cloud-level outage confirmed (console shows region status = degraded): expedite to larger weight shifts and consider global fallback (DNS TTL pre-warming recommended).

Canary traffic shift procedure (manual steps - preferred for first incidents)
Prereqs: have infractl or route53 console access, logs open, and IC approval.
1) Notify channels: #ops-incident, customer-alerts (if required), legal if major customers impacted.
2) Set edge circuit-breaker to short-circuit for unhealthy hosts: update Envoy route config: 
   - action: set circuit_breakers -> max_connections: 50, max_pending_requests: 20, max_retries: 0, consecutive_5xx: 3 
   - command (infractl): infractl envoy update --route default --circuit-breaker "max_connections=50,max_pending_requests=20,max_retries=0,consecutive_5xx=3"
3) Canary step 1: Set Route53 weighted records: primary=99, standby=1 (TTL=60). Confirm via dig from two regions: 
   - dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
   - curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:<standby-ip> https://api.redwood.ai/health
4) Observe 5m window for error-rate and latency increase in standby. Watch for cache stampede signs (sudden spike in model-serving backend CPU or KV misses).
5) If stable, progress to 95/5, then 75/25, then 100 in 10–15 minute increments depending on traffic and customer impact.

Full failover (if canary fails or immediate cutoff required):
- If standby region shows sustained degradation at any step, rollback weights to previous stable values immediately and rollback circuit-breaker to default.
- If primary region is unrecoverable, set Route53 weights to 0/100 (primary/standby). Update global routing rules and CDN origin priorities.
- Announce customer status: update status.redwood.ai and send out templated incident messages.

Rollback checklist (after failed canary):
- Reset route53 weights to last known-good (document weight history per incident)
- Restore Envoy circuit-breaker to previous config: infractl envoy update --route default --reset-circuit-breaker
- Run cache-warming jobs in primary (if primary coming back) to reduce cold-start amplification
- Record timing for postmortem (when weight changed, when rollback issued, metrics observed)

Operational knobs and gotchas:
- DNS TTLs: clients and CDNs may ignore low TTLs; expect 1–10 minute propagation variance. Use application-level header for clients when possible (cache-control for edge).
- Cache storms: when shifting traffic from primary to standby, the standby may see large numbers of cache misses; consider pre-warming key prefixes for high-volume tenants.
- BGP community toggles: if using direct routing, ensure network runbook for announcing/withdrawing prefixes is handy. Mistakes here are high-impact.
- Circuit-breakers at multiple layers: API gateway, edge proxy, and service-side breakers must be coordinated to avoid masking or amplifying failures.

Automation snippets (ideas for infra team):
- infractl runbook apply --canary --from primary=us-east --to standby=us-west --weights 1,5,25,100 --pause 300s --rollback-on "p95_latency>500ms || error_rate>2%"
- Route53 API example (Python):
   import boto3
   r53 = boto3.client('route53')
   # update weighted record code here (omitted for runbook brevity)

On-call notes (freeform):
- 2026-02-24 incident: shifted to standby too quickly (jumped from 1% to 100%); observed KV cache storm, CPU trip on model-serving. Action: adjust canary cadence to include cache pre-warm step.
- Hint: when moving >10% traffic, trigger k/v warmers for the top-1000 keys per tenant.
- Use small synthetic load against standby to validate cold caches before moving customer traffic.

Post-incident follow-ups (POAM):
- (P1) Add an automated cache-warm pre-step in canary shift (infra ticket: SRE-4898)
- (P2) Lower default Route53 TTL for critical hostnames from 300 -> 60 seconds and document exceptions (product must sign off)
- (P3) Add canary automation with safety gates measured on both p95 latency and global error budget remaining
- (P4) Run quarterly chaos exercise for region-level failure and document time-to-stable metric

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we maintain a global sticky session for customers with ws connections during partial regional shifts? Need product/engineering discussion.
- What SLA notification wording is acceptable for warm-standby initiation? Work with legal/CS.

Appendix: quick commands (placeholders - adapt to environment)
- Check region health (from SRE bastion): curl -sS https://api-us-east.redwood.ai/health | jq .status
- Update Route53 weights (AWS CLI skeleton): aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch file://weight-change.json
- Envoy config reload (infractl): infractl envoy reload --service frontend --config /tmp/new-config.yaml
- Validate DNS from remote: dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep this doc short and actionable. Save long discussions for confluence page linked above.
- Iterate after next DR drill.

End of draft.

Change log:
- 2026-02-24: added cache storm mitigation note after real incident.
- 2025-11-12: initial draft created.
